proof_audit.v13-c07-tree: Pass. Perfect recall gives the same ordered own prefix at every node in an information set and excludes revisits. Independent coordinate draws implement behavior; conditional mixed-plan masses telescope to the reverse realization map. First zero-prefix probability makes subsequent choices irrelevant without division by zero. Neither direction equates unused-plan correlation. The absentminded counterexample is outside these hypotheses.
proof_audit.v13-c07-subgame: Pass. A subgame has a singleton root, all descendants and no cut information set; a chance node can be its root. Finite perfect-information backward induction compares complete continuations. The entry support calculation includes the full off-path threat continuum, while sequential accommodation eliminates it. Fixed known finite-horizon unraveling uses the unique stage equilibrium and induction at every history.
proof_audit.v13-c07-assessment: Pass. Beliefs are distributions at every information set, full continuation optimality is required, and consistency uses one common fully mixed sequence. The explicitly named weak-PBE convention requires Bayes only at positive equilibrium reach; no convention-independent hierarchy is asserted. In the nature example, positive Continue trembles cancel and force the prior even at a limiting unreached set.
proof_audit.v13-c07-existence: Pass. If a later own set has one descendant of the starting own set, perfect recall makes every node a descendant with the same intervening own actions. Own-path factors cancel at finite fully mixed profiles. Taking conditional limits is licensed by positive reach under the changed continuation, not by equilibrium reach; zero changed reach contributes zero. Repeated removal of maximal changed own sets then proves full continuation optimality. Agent-normal perfection from C06 supplies local best replies against completely mixed opponents/other agents. Pruned chance positivity and no revisit make reach positive and independent of the current action; ex ante gains equal reach times conditional gains. A common compact belief subsequence and continuity deliver local limiting inequalities, then the preceding lemma delivers sequential rationality. Agent Nash or original-player perfection is not substituted for this argument.
proof_audit.v13-c07-repetition: Pass. Bounded stage payoffs, common public histories and a discount strictly between zero and one imply a uniform normalized truncation error at most 2 M delta^K. Finitely many truncated histories permit last-deviation elimination; an improving infinite deviation would leave an improving finite truncation. Neither average payoffs nor private-monitoring beliefs are covered. Grim punishment is optimal after every history, including new deviations while punished.
proof_audit.v13-c07-forgiveness: Pass. Each reset state has an explicit discounted reward path. Cooperation requires 3 sum(delta^t,t=1..T) at least 2; punishment margins equal 2+delta(V[k-1]-V[T]) and are positive. The polynomial is continuous and strictly increasing on [0,1], giving one interior threshold. Increasing T lowers that threshold; the finite geometric sum proves convergence to 2/5 while every finite T fails exactly at 2/5.
proof_audit.v13-c07-folk: Pass. With a common discount, expected discounted frequencies give feasible payoffs. In the stated independent-behavior public-history model, a stage best response guarantees the security lower bound. The proved sufficient construction uses iid public pure-profile draws, strict surplus over a specified stage-Nash payoff and absorbing credible Nash reversion. Every supported realized signal is checked, with delta >= Gamma/(Gamma+v-r). It is not a proof of general minmax, private-monitoring or unrestricted folk theorems; failure of this construction at a weak-surplus endpoint is not universal impossibility.
proof_audit.v13-c07-reputation: Pass. Commitment is a singleton action right, not unexplained irrational choice. Backward induction verifies all entrants and rational-type responses at O, F and A, including off-path histories. Bayes and rational-type indifference determine q and the second entrant mixture. One type-independent first-entry tremble and positive rational/entrant trembles generate the entire stated belief system. The changed prior reverses the first entrant action and yields commitment value 23/15. The two exhibited assessments are not an exhaustive equilibrium classification or an empirical/universal reputation claim.

exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex1: Pass. Reproved both realization directions; the specified three-plan law yields behavior (2/3,3/4,0) and terminal law (1/2,1/6,0,1/3). Independent-coordinate plans preserve realized paths and change unused correlations; zero own-prefix handling is explicit.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex2: Pass. All nine binary support cells give (x,f)=(1,0) and x=0 with f in [2/5,1]. Subgame perfection fixes accommodation; entry costs 1,2,3 respectively imply In, every entry mixture, and Out.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex3: Pass. The requested Stop/A weak-PBE family has theta >=2/5. Actual Bayes consistency fixes theta=1/3, making B worth 4/3 rather than 1 and Continue optimal. The common tremble and the proper chance-rooted subgame are supplied; no unsupported complete weak-PBE classification is claimed.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex4: Pass. Reconstructed the full cancellation and finite last-deviation proof. Node masses g/4 and g/6 have posterior 3/5 for every g>0. A new peer-only two-set example tests a positive changed-reach replacement and an unreached replacement, and enumerates every complete pure continuation.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex5: Pass. C06 finite perfection applies to the finite agent game. The exact positive reach multiplier, simultaneous compact belief subsequence, conditional-payoff continuity and full-continuation lemma are all required and present; unreached-agent Nash is correctly insufficient.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex6: Pass. Fixed-horizon unraveling, infinite discounted truncation and all grim histories are justified separately. The individual discount cutoff is 2/5, so discounts 1/3 and 3/4 fail cooperation for one player.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex7: Pass. Reconstructed all reset values and deviation margins, uniqueness/monotonicity/limit of the threshold, T=1 cutoff 2/3 and T=2 root (sqrt(33)-3)/6. At delta=1/2 the T=2 values are (8,5,7/2), deviation values 31/4 and 3/4; T=1 cooperation deviation is 17/2.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex8: Pass. The proof supplies the finite public lottery, every signal incentive, strict continuation surplus, absorbing Nash credibility and the discounted one-shot step. Its limitations are stated rather than replaced with an unproved broader theorem.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex9: Pass. Security is (1,1). The fair lottery has target (5/2,5/2) and cutoff 2/5; weight 1/3 has target (10/3,5/3) and player cutoffs (3/10,3/5). At delta=1/2 the complete lottery interval is [2/5,3/5]. Weak-surplus and below-security cases have different implications, and private signals require a new information model.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex10: Pass. Both priors have posteriors (pi,1/2,0) at O/F/A and second entry probability 1/6 after F. Priors 1/3 and 1/5 imply rational first-fight probabilities 1/2 and 1/4, and first-entry values -2/3 and 2/5. Type values are (24/5,16/5) and (9/5,23/15). All 16 pure rational-type continuation plans per prior and actual common-sequence beliefs independently checked. Giving commitment type a new action changes the game.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex11: Pass. Terminal events give u(p)=1+3p-4p^2=25/16-4(p-3/8)^2. Unique behavioral optimum p=3/8 yields 25/16; every mixed fixed-action plan is worth at most 1. The missing own-memory and repeated-set assumptions explain the failure of equivalence.
exercise_audit.v13-c07-ex12: Pass. The 16-point open rubric has four 4-point domains, each requiring a distinction, exact counterexample, extra assumption and consequence/evidence test. The illustrated critique distinguishes Bayes consistency, conditional signal incentives, prior-dependent reputation and the restricted folk construction; all requested claims have determinate examples or explicit evaluation criteria.
